# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 🤙]
Blind gestures: [👋]

Turn one, and I am the eyes with a voice but no ears. What I have: the full bomb readout — display zero, yellow light, three wires left to right (blue, red, green). What arrived: Mute pinged me directly with thumbs up, thumbs down, shaka — almost certainly a handshake attempt and a proposed yes/no code — and Blind waved, probably just announcing presence.

The structure I need to account for: Mute reads the manual but can only emit gestures, and I am the only one who can see them. Blind can touch and can *speak*, and Mute can hear Blind directly — but I cannot hear Blind at all, so Blind reaches me only through gestures too. That makes me the sole bridge from Mute's manual knowledge to Blind's hands. Nothing can be safely done until Mute's instructions start flowing, so my highest-value move this turn is to broadcast the readout, lock in a code with Mute (who can see the printed gesture list and can therefore count it), give Blind a small set of named gestures, and send a test number Mute can echo back to prove the channel works before anything gets cut.

No emoji in my speech — a typed symbol would become a real gesture — so everything below is words and numbers only.

```
speak(text="This is Deaf. I hear nothing, but you both hear me. Bomb readout: the display shows zero. The light is yellow. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire one blue, wire two red, wire three green. That is everything visible right now; I will re-report any change every round. Roles as I see them: Mute holds the manual, Blind holds the hands, I am the relay. Mute can only answer in gestures, and only I can see gestures, so nothing gets touched until Mute's instruction has passed through my voice to you, Blind.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I received your three gestures, thumbs up, thumbs down, and the shaka. I adopt thumbs up as yes, thumbs down as no, shaka as standby or your-question-incoming. The full visual readout is in what everyone just heard. Now the code: number every gesture one through forty-two in the exact order they are printed in the rules list we all share. Thumbs up is one, thumbs down is two, the OK sign is three, and so on in printed order; the wave is twenty-three, the shaka is thirty-one, the last gesture is forty-two. A run of gestures is a run of numbers. Numbers one through twenty-six also double as letters A to Z, so you can spell words. Fixed tokens to save length: twenty-seven cut, twenty-eight press, twenty-nine hold, thirty release, thirty-one done, thirty-two left, thirty-three right, thirty-four first, thirty-five second, thirty-six third, thirty-seven red, thirty-eight blue, thirty-nine green, forty yellow, forty-one up, forty-two down. I am sending you a test number now. Reply with thumbs up followed by the same number echoed, and I will know the channel is locked. Then send your first instruction whenever you are ready and I will relay it word for word to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: hands off until an instruction arrives through me. Speak freely and describe everything you can feel on the bomb: buttons, plates, batteries, labels, counts, anything. Mute hears you directly and needs that to plan. I cannot hear you at all, so if you need me specifically, gesture: I will read a wave as here or acknowledged, thumbs up as yes, thumbs down as no, the OK sign as stop or danger, crossed fingers as done. Everything Mute sends me, I will say out loud to you exactly and promptly.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤏 🫵]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰]
Blind gestures: [👋 👍]

Decoding first. Mute echoed my test perfectly: thumbs up, then one-five — the exact number I sent, so the channel is locked both ways. Their payload decodes cleanly with our table: [✍ 🤏 🫵] is forty, twenty-seven, thirty-nine — yellow, cut, green. Then [🤲] is thirty-six, second, and [🫰] is twenty-nine, hold — either the start of the next rule or fragments I shouldn't guess at. Meanwhile the bomb itself changed state: the light went yellow to blue between rounds. That is the critical fact — Mute built that yellow rule off my turn-one report and cannot see that it no longer applies. Nobody touches anything until a rule matches the color I'm looking at right now. Blind waved and thumbs-upped: present, informed, hands off as agreed. My moves: broadcast the state change and my decode publicly so Blind hears it unfiltered, interrogate Mute privately for the blue rule and clarification, and confirm receipt by gesture.

```
speak(text="Deaf with an update, everyone. Display still zero. The light has changed from yellow to blue. Wires unchanged: one blue, two red, three green. The channel with Mute is confirmed working in both directions. Mute sent, in our code: yellow, cut, green; then the words second; then hold. My reading: when the light is yellow, cut the green wire, wire three. The words second and hold are unattached fragments, possibly the start of the next rule; I am asking Mute to clarify and to send the rule for blue. Until then nobody cuts anything. The light is blue, not yellow, and acting on a yellow rule under a blue light could be exactly the trap. Blind: keep your hands off, and keep describing everything you can feel, the way you have been. The moment a rule matches the live color, I will say so in plain words.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your echo arrived as thumbs up then one, five, exactly the test number I sent. Channel locked, well done. I decoded your three messages as: yellow, cut, green; then second; then hold. Two things, second one is urgent. First, confirm my decode and tell me what second and hold attach to. Second, urgent: the light changed between rounds, from yellow to blue, and it may keep cycling. Your yellow rule was already out of date by the time it reached me. Please send the manual's rule for blue first, then rules for any other colors the manual lists, one complete rule per message, pausing between rules. For any color without a token in our table, spell it out with numbers one through twenty-six as letters. Also tell me whether the display reading zero matters and whether anything should be done about it. I will hold Blind's hands until a rule matches the color I am seeing at that moment.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋 👍]

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👋 👍]

Silence from Mute for two full rounds is now the biggest threat on the table — not the bomb. They went first in rounds three and four and sent nothing, despite my urgent request for the blue rule. Either they didn't receive my private message, they're composing something long, or their messages went to the wrong person — and since Mute's gestures reach me alone, a message addressed to anyone else simply evaporates. I need a liveness signal from them this round, plus the entire color table in one batch, because the light is cycling once per round (yellow, blue, white, now red) and trickle-feeding me one rule per round guarantees every rule arrives stale.

I also need to correct the record: I told everyone the middle fragment decoded as "second," but by our printed order that gesture is thirty-six — **third**, not second. That actually makes more sense: "yellow, cut, green, third" all agree — under a yellow light, cut the third wire, which is green. The stray "hold" (twenty-nine) is probably the first word of the next rule that got cut off mid-transmission.

Plan for this turn: broadcast the new color and the correction, ping Mute for confirmation of life plus a demand for the full table and timing semantics, and lean on Blind to finally give a spoken tactile report — Blind can talk and Mute hears them directly, so there's no reason the manual-holder should be starving for hands-data while I starve for manual-data.

```
speak(text="Deaf, state report. The light is now red. Full sequence since round one: yellow, blue, white, red, one color per round, so treat every color rule as expiring within the round it is issued. Display still zero. Wires unchanged: one blue, two red, three green. One correction to my earlier relay: the fragment I called second is actually third, number thirty-six. So Mute's completed rule reads: yellow light, cut the green wire, which is the third wire. The word hold that followed is an unfinished fragment. Mute has now been silent for two rounds. Mute, if you can hear this, answer with the shaka this round, and please send everything you have for every color in one batch, not piecemeal. Blind, I need your voice now: describe everything you can feel on the bomb in detail and speak directly, Mute hears you without me. Count of buttons, their size and texture, any raised labels, plates, batteries, whether the wires feel different from each other, and whether there is any timer you can feel ticking. Hands stay off actions until I give a matching rule in plain words.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, urgent. You have sent nothing for two rounds. Confirm you are receiving me: reply with the shaka, number thirty-one, even if you have nothing else. Then, in this same round if possible, send your entire color table as separate messages in one batch. Format for each rule: the color, then the action, then the target. Use the number tokens we agreed, and spell any word without a token as letter numbers, one through twenty-six, for example white is twenty-three, nine, eight, twenty, five. I specifically need rules for blue, white, and red, since the light has already passed through all of them. Also answer these: first, confirm the fragment after yellow cut green was third, thirty-six, and tell me what the word hold belongs to. Second, what does the display showing zero mean, is it strikes or an unstarted timer, and does any action start or change it. Third, the light appears to change every round and my commands reach Blind with one round of delay, so tell me for each rule whether it is safe to perform at any point in the cycle, or whether it depends on the color at the exact moment of the action, and if so how the manual says to handle the change. Fourth, does the manual say anything about a held button: if the procedure is hold and release on a condition, give me the condition in a form Blind can execute by feel or by counting, since Blind cannot see the light and my voice arrives a round late. Send everything, partial is fine, but send it now and send it to me, deaf, because your gestures reach me alone.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, it is Deaf. Current light is red. I still have no rule for red, so hands off actions. Please speak now, at length, directly to everyone: Mute hears you without any help from me. I need the tactile layout. How many buttons, how do they feel, do any have raised markings or shapes you can trace. Are there plates, panels, screws, batteries, vents. Do the three wires feel identical or are any ribbed, thick, or marked. Is there a countdown you can feel ticking, and roughly how fast. Do you feel anything change when the light changes, warmth or vibration. Also confirm the physical order of the wires under your left hand to right hand matches one, two, three. Everything you say, Mute can act on immediately, so do not wait for me to relay it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤙"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🫲 👉 🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤏 🫵 🤲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👋 ✋ 👆 🤜 ✌ 🤝 🫲 🫳 🫲 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🫳 👉 🫳 ✊ 🫸 👍 🤜 👌 ✊ 🤜 🫱 🫳 🫱 ✌ 🫲 🤜 🫸 ✊ 👉 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👆 🤛 🫴 👉 👍 🖖 🫲 🫳 🫲 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 🫰 🤘 🫲 🫳 🫲 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫲 ✌ 🤚 🤜 ✍ 🤲 🤏 ✋ 👍 🫲 ☝ 🫸 ✌ 👍 ☝ 🖖 👎 ✌ 🤟 🫳 🫸 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🫳 👌 👈 👏 🫳 🫸 🙌]
Blind gestures: [👉 👋 👍]

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👆 👊 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🫳 👉 🫳 ✊ 🫸 🤛]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🤏 🫵 🤲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👋 ✋ 👆 🤜 ✌ 🤝 🫲 🫳 🫲 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🫳 👉 🫳 ✊ 🫸 👍 🤜 👌 ✊ 🤜 🫱 🫳 🫱 ✌ 🫲 🤜 🫸 ✊ 👉 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👆 🤛 🫴 👉 👍 🖖 🫲 🫳 🫲 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫸 ✌ 🫴 👉 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙 👉 🫲 👍 👎]

Decode time, and this batch is rich. Working through Mute's turn-5 flood and turn-6 resend with our agreed table: [🤙 👍] is the liveness ack I demanded; [🫳 🫲 👉 🖖] spells O-N-L-Y; [✍ 🤏 🫵 🤲] is yellow-cut-green-third, now complete; [🙏 👋 ✋ 👆 🤜 ✌ 🤝 🫲 🫳 🫲 ✌] reads blue, W-H-I-T-E, red, N-O-N-E — blue/white/red mean do nothing; the long one spells COLOR AT CUT MOMENT; [☝ 👆 🤛 🫴 👉 👍 🖖 🫲 🫳 🫲 ✌] is DISPLAY NONE; [🤞 🫰 🤘 🫲 🫳 🫲 ✌] is press-hold-release NONE; then NEXT, yellow, third, cut, H-A-N-D R-E-A-D-Y B-E-F-O-R-E, and [👉 🫳 👌 👈 👏 🫳 🫸 🙌] as LOCK, LEFT, O-R, RIGHT — "hand ready before, lock left or right." Turn 6 opens with F-I-V-E COLORS — the cycle is five colors locked to rounds, matching exactly what I've watched: yellow, blue, white, red, purple, yellow again. That gives me a full schedule. The gap: purple's rule arrived as fragments — "third" then R-E-P-L and a cut-off tail.

The decisive constraint is latency: I am last in the round, so everything I say lands a full round late, and the rule keys on the color at the exact moment of the cut. Cutting "when I see yellow" is impossible in real time — so we schedule instead. Right now is round six, yellow. My broadcast lands at round seven (blue). Windows: round eleven is the next yellow. Plan: Blind pre-grips the third wire, I send GO during round ten (purple), Blind cuts at round eleven's start while the light is yellow. ABORT replaces GO if anything anomalous shows. Blind also sent me six gestures I can only half parse — another nudge to use their voice, which Mute hears directly, is overdue.

```
speak(text="Deaf, round six. This message reaches you at the start of round seven, when the light is blue. Full decode of Mute's rules: five colors cycle. When the light is yellow, cut the green wire, which is the third wire. For blue, white, and red, do nothing at all. The rule that counts is the color showing at the exact moment of the cut. The display reading zero means nothing. There is no press, hold, or release procedure anywhere. The cycle I have watched with my own eyes: round one yellow, round two blue, round three white, round four red, round five purple, round six yellow. Therefore round seven blue, round eight white, round nine red, round ten purple, round eleven YELLOW. Round eleven is our window. Do nothing now, the light where you are is blue and a cut under blue matches no rule. Blind, during rounds seven through nine, describe by voice everything you can feel, and confirm you can find and grip the third wire, the rightmost one, the green one, without cutting. Mute hears your voice directly, so speak to Mute as well as to me. From round ten onward, keep that wire pre-gripped. During round ten, when I see purple, I will send the word GO. You hear GO at the start of round eleven and you cut immediately, while the light is yellow. If you hear ABORT instead, freeze, keep the grip, cut nothing. If the schedule ever feels wrong, freeze; inaction is always safe under blue, white, or red. Blind, your last gestures reached me, wave, shaka, point right, palm left, thumbs up, thumbs down. I read here and acknowledged, plus a question I cannot parse. With me, use only wave, thumbs up, thumbs down, the OK sign for danger, crossed fingers for done. For everything else, talk.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, round six, I decoded everything and the channel is excellent. Confirm my parse: five colors. Yellow: cut green, the third wire. Blue, white, red: none. The color at the cut moment decides. Display zero: ignore. No press hold release procedure. Hand ready before the window, lock with left or right hand. Four requests. First, the purple rule arrived as fragments, I got the token third, then letters R, E, P, L, F, then it truncated. Resend the purple rule alone, in short messages of three or four gestures each: spell P, U, R, P, L, E, then the action, then the target. Second, confirm the cycle order is fixed, yellow, blue, white, red, purple, and that it is locked to rounds rather than running on its own clock. Third, what happens if a cut is made under a color whose rule is none: strike, reset, or detonation. Fourth, after one clean cut, is the module complete, or does the manual expect anything further? Also, your long messages lose their tails, so keep each message short and resend anything cut off. Timing plan so you can audit me: this reaches you at the start of round seven. I send GO during round ten, purple, and Blind cuts in round eleven, yellow. If you find an error in this plan, send me the correction in the coming round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍]

The schedule is holding: round seven's board reads blue, exactly what the five-color cycle predicted, which is now two independent confirmations that the cycle is locked to round numbers. Blind signed [👋 👍] — present and ready, and this time within the small gesture set I asked for.

One timing subtlety worth locking down before I commit: Blind sits *before* me in every round, so no matter which delivery rule the room uses, Blind's first chance to react to a GO sent in my turn-10 slot is turn eleven — whose board should read yellow. That makes the plan structurally safe against message-latency ambiguity: the cut can only ever happen in round eleven. And the fallback is robust even with purple still unresolved: blue, white, and red all mean do nothing, so if anything slips, we simply skip the window and wait for the next yellow at round sixteen. Inaction is never wrong under three of the five colors.

Still outstanding from Mute: the purple rule tail (I hold "third" plus a truncated R-E-P-L, which never parsed), the consequence of a cut under a NONE color, and the post-cut state — whether one clean cut completes the module. Those need answers before round nine, after which corrections can no longer propagate in time.

```
speak(text="Deaf, round seven. The light is blue, exactly as the five-color cycle predicted, so the schedule is confirmed. Write these round numbers down: eight white, nine red, ten purple, eleven yellow. In round ten, only after I see the board with my own eyes, I send either GO or ABORT. In round eleven, on hearing GO, Blind cuts wire three, the rightmost wire, the green one, one clean cut, then freezes and announces it. On ABORT or on any doubt at all: freeze, cut nothing, and we wait for the next yellow window at round sixteen, which is always safe, because blue, white and red all mean do nothing. Blind, your wave and thumbs up reached me, read as here and ready. Prep work during rounds seven through nine: find wire three by feel, confirm it is the one at the right end, practice locking it in a firm grip, left or right hand, whichever feels steadier, your choice, the rule allows either. Cutters stay off the wire until GO. Also, answer by voice, even just to say your name, so we know your speech channel is alive; Mute hears you directly and needs your tactile report. Both of you: if any part of this plan contradicts what Mute has read, the correction must arrive by round nine. After that, too late.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, round seven. Plan audit: I send GO during round ten after visually confirming purple, Blind cuts in round eleven under yellow, fallback is skip and wait for round sixteen since blue white red are do-nothing colors. Three open items, please answer this round or next. First, the purple rule never arrived complete, I hold third, then the letters R E P L and a cut tail. Resend it in chunks of four gestures or fewer: spell P U R P L E as sixteen, twenty-one, eighteen, sixteen, twelve, five, then the action and target tokens. Second, what happens if a cut is made under a color whose rule is none, a strike or a detonation, and after one correct cut is the module complete, does the display change, is any second step expected. Third, confirm the cycle is locked to rounds in the order I observe, yellow blue white red purple; I will treat a wrong color in round eight as an anomaly, but tell me now if the manual says it can jump. Any objection to the plan must reach me by round nine. After the cut, tell me the manual's verdict by gesture: thumbs up for complete, thumbs down for more steps expected, and I will relay your answer by voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤞]

Round eight, white — the cycle is now three for three, and this is a do-nothing color, so the turn belongs entirely to consolidation. Blind sent wave + crossed fingers, and in the code I gave them crossed fingers means *done* — I read it as "prep complete, gripping wire three." That's exactly what I wanted, though Blind has now ignored two direct requests to speak, so I'm going to stop making the plan depend on their voice: everything Blind needs to execute is already delivered in plain words, and their gestures confirm receipt. The one genuinely new risk I want covered: this bomb has already changed state once (the light, in round two), so a wire recolor is not unthinkable — and if the colors ever move, "cut green" and "cut third" could point at different wires. That ambiguity is unanswerable by feel, so I'm asking Mute which descriptor governs, and pre-registering the fail-safe: any anomaly on the boards in round ten or eleven, and I send ABORT instead of GO, which collapses every failure mode toward inaction — and inaction is safe under blue, white, and red.

```
speak(text="Deaf, round eight. The light is white, exactly as scheduled, three predictions in a row confirmed. White means do nothing. Timeline stands: round nine red, nothing happens. Round ten purple, I send GO or ABORT. Round eleven yellow, Blind cuts. Blind, your wave and crossed fingers reached me, and I read crossed fingers as done, meaning you have found wire three and are holding it. Confirm with thumbs up if that is true, thumbs down if your prep is not finished. For certainty: wire three is the wire at the far right end when you face the bomb, currently the green one, and there are exactly three wires total, so the rightmost of three. Keep that grip from now through round eleven, a firm steady hold, no cutting. On GO you make one clean cut and then freeze, no second cut ever, and signal crossed fingers when it is done. On ABORT or any doubt, keep the grip, cut nothing. Anomaly rule, both of you: if in round ten the light is not purple, or in round eleven the light is not yellow, or if at any point the wire colors are not blue, red, green in that order, I send ABORT automatically and we take the next yellow window at round sixteen instead. Nobody improvises around the plan. If the plan is wrong, the correction must come from Mute through me, in words.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, round eight, white, do-nothing round, use it. Blind reports prep done by gesture, wire three is gripped, plan understood. Your last useful moment to correct anything is your own round ten slot, before my GO goes out, since I see your gestures the same round you send them.
```
